title: Observability: tag latency histograms with profile_id + sku; add scheduler_queue_ms
author: Omar El-Sayed
description: Context: As part of the Hardware tuning profiles pack rollout we need to be able to compare latency distributions across profiles and hardware SKUs (and quickly answer “is this regression specific to a profile default or to a fleet/hardware slice?”). Today our request latency histograms do not include profile_id nor detected GPU SKU, which makes canary and post-incident triage slower and forces manual correlation via logs. This PR adds two bounded labels (profile_id, sku) to the existing latency histograms and introduces a new histogram metric scheduler_queue_ms to explicitly measure queueing time (time spent waiting for scheduler admission) as distinct from compute time. Changes: (1) Add labels profile_id and sku to runtime latency histograms (end_to_end, prefill, decode) emitted from the serving runtime metrics layer. (2) Add runtime_scheduler_queue_ms histogram (ms) recorded at the scheduler boundary for each request / microbatch admission; tag with the same label set to allow apples-to-apples comparisons. (3) Cardinality guardrails: sku is normalized to a small set (H100, B200, L40S, UNKNOWN); profile_id is required to be a short runtime-defined identifier (e.g., h100-default-v1) and defaults to "unknown" when profiles are disabled/unavailable. (4) Wire labels into tracing span -> metrics bridge so dashboards can pivot consistently; update metric docs and add unit tests to lock label sets (prevent accidental extra labels). Rollout/compatibility: Existing dashboards that query latency histograms without labels should continue to work (Prometheus aggregation still works, but callers that do exact label matching will need updates). This is a runtime-only change; no control-plane changes required. Follow-ups: Observability-pack dashboards will be updated in a separate PR to add profile adoption panels and p95 by profile_id/sku.
commits: metrics: plumb detected sku + active profile_id into metrics context
metrics: add (profile_id, sku) labels to latency histograms
scheduler: record scheduler_queue_ms at admission boundary
tests: lock histogram label sets + add prom snapshot
docs: update runtime metrics reference for profile pack rollout
conversation: Allison Grant (review): Adding labels is good, but we need to be explicit about cardinality. Can we guarantee sku is normalized and profile_id is bounded? Also please document the exact label set for each histogram so the dashboards team can update queries safely. Omar El-Sayed (author): Yep. Added normalization in sku_detect (H100/B200/L40S/UNKNOWN). For profile_id, it’s taken from the profile pack loader and defaults to "unknown" when disabled; added a unit test that fails if any other labels are added. Also added a short section to runtime/metrics/README.md with the full label sets and example PromQL. Julian Moore (review): Where exactly is scheduler_queue_ms measured? Want to ensure we’re measuring queueing, not including prefill tokenization or frontend time. Omar El-Sayed (author): Measured at scheduler admission boundary: start timestamp when request is enqueued for scheduler, end timestamp when it’s admitted into an execution slot (right before microbatch formation). It excludes frontend/gateway and excludes compute; includes backpressure wait. Added a code comment and a trace annotation so we can validate in flame charts. Noah Patel (review): Please confirm this won’t break existing alerts that match on exact label sets. We’ve had this issue before. Omar El-Sayed (author): Existing alerts aggregate over histogram buckets; queries without label selectors still work. I did find two internal alert rules in runtime-oncall that used an explicit label list; I updated those in the same PR to aggregate by (le, route) plus the new labels via sum without selectors. Sean Gallagher (review): Any risk this increases metrics volume enough to trip ingestion limits during canary? Omar El-Sayed (author): Estimated additional series: latency_histograms * (profile_id x sku). In Hosted we expect <= 6 active profile_ids at a time; sku is 3-4 values. That’s within our current budget; also added a note that profile_id must remain bounded and is not allowed to include customer identifiers. Approving with that guardrail. Allison Grant (approval): Approved. Please ping me when the dashboard PR is up so we can land them together for the rollout checklist.
release_notes: Runtime now exports latency histograms labeled by active profile_id and detected GPU sku, plus a new scheduler_queue_ms histogram to separate queueing from compute. This improves profile pack canary visibility and post-incident triage.
